title: rubus fruticosus subsp. pallidus
intro: Rubus fruticosus subsp. pallidus, commonly known as the pale bramble, is a subspecies of the blackberry bush that is native to Europe and Western Asia. It is a shrub with edible fruits and has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties that may help to protect against cardiovascular disease, improve digestion, and boost the immune system. The therapeutic actions of Rubus fruticosus subsp. pallidus are attributed to its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce inflammation, and exhibit antioxidant activity, which may contribute to its use in the treatment of various health conditions, including diabetes and cancer. The bioactive constituents of Rubus fruticosus subsp. pallidus include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and ellagitannins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
